model: Orbital Economy v7.7.14 Recalibration candidate r1
note: Task 035 recalibration fragment. Updates exactly the three parameter annotations required by TASK_RU §2. Values follow the owner decision after sensitivity analysis; Target Labor Tightness is unchanged but explicitly marked as a key long-horizon wage parameter.

Power Operating Reserve Factor.role: Generation operating-reserve factor, recalibrated from 1.02 to 1.10.
Power Operating Reserve Factor.effect: Generation capacity is planned at 110% of expected industrial load. This removes the thinnest reserve margin in the model and moves the system away from the energy-deficit threshold where small demand/model errors caused chronic shortage.
Power Operating Reserve Factor.evidence: docs/research/SENSITIVITY_2026-10-10_RU.md: Power Operating Reserve Factor is one of the strongest nonlinear parameters; on the 20-year pass, lowering the old 1.02 reserve produced chronic energy deficit and large output/price effects. Owner decision 2026-10-11: recalibrate to 1.10.

Labor Participation Share.role: Dimensionless share of population counted as labor force, recalibrated from 0.50 to 0.52.
Labor Participation Share.effect: Labor Force = Population × Labor Participation Share for each region. The 0.52 calibration moves colony A off the labor-shortage edge while preserving the intended labor-market mechanism; labor-demand signal initial stocks are recalibrated consistently to 14.56 / 4.42.
Labor Participation Share.evidence: docs/research/SENSITIVITY_2026-10-10_RU.md: participation is strongly nonlinear and its effect grows on the 20-year horizon; owner 80-year calibration decision on 2026-10-11 selected 0.52 to remove the shortage-edge behavior while keeping wages stable for roughly two decades.

Target Labor Tightness.role: KEY PARAMETER: target ratio of smoothed labor demand to labor force; value remains 0.95.
Target Labor Tightness.effect: Sets the long-run wage equilibrium target: tightness above 0.95 raises wages and below 0.95 lowers them. The value is unchanged in v7.7.14 but is explicitly marked key because sensitivity grows materially on long horizons.
Target Labor Tightness.evidence: docs/research/SENSITIVITY_2026-10-10_RU.md: Target Labor Tightness grows from moderate short-horizon sensitivity to a strong long-horizon wage driver; owner decision 2026-10-11 keeps 0.95 unchanged and marks it as a key parameter.
